haiku-low.q1: Held for 10 minutes. Unclaimed holds are expired by a timer every minute and the stock goes back on sale. A late claim re-takes the stock only if every line is still free.
haiku-low.q2: Before. Inventory reserves stock first, then Payment charges. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment is requested, and the cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q3: The provider idempotency key set to the order id. A retried charge returns the original charge instead of a second one. Payment also has one payment row per order id.
haiku-low.q4: Inventory publishes ClaimFailed. Order is marked CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and emails the customer. Payment automatically refunds the full amount, and Order later marks REFUNDED. The cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q5: Only when Order publishes OrderConfirmed after the stock is claimed, and Cart empties itself. If checkout fails, the cart is left unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service is the coordinator. Its orders table stores each order's status, which records how far that checkout has got.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment saves the result and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined, which Order receives as an event.
haiku-low.q8: Payment's webhook_inbox has a unique provider event id, so duplicates get a 200 and are ignored. Every handler also checks the current status or keys first.
haiku-low.q9: Order receives PaymentDeclined, marks the order PAYMENT_DECLINED, and calls Inventory over HTTP to release the hold. The cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory's claim checks the hold. If it is still valid, or lapsed but every line is still free, the order is fulfilled. Otherwise ClaimFailed triggers a refund.
haiku-low.q11: The refund is saved as REFUND_FAILED with an attempt count and next retry time, in Payment's refunds table. A timer retries it, ops are alerted after N attempts, and it is never deleted.
haiku-low.q12: Order's OrderConfirmed event, published after the stock is claimed. The Cart service reacts to it by emptying the cart.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If unclaimed, a timer (every minute) expires the hold and the stock goes back on sale.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before charging. If any line is short, nothing is reserved (all-or-nothing), StockShort lists the short items, order is REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK, no payment is requested, and the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key (order id) sent to the provider: a retry returns the original charge instead of a second one. Payment also has a unique payment row per order id.
sonnet.q4: Inventory publishes ClaimFailed; the order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is emailed, nothing ships, and a full automatic refund is requested (RefundRequested), ending in REFUNDED. The cart stays as it was.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only when the order is confirmed (on OrderConfirmed). When checkout fails (short stock, declined, or late-success cancellation) the cart is left unchanged.
sonnet.q6: Order is the coordinator that moves it along on replies/events. The record is the order's status in Order's own database (orders table).
sonnet.q7: The provider calls Payment's webhook endpoint; Payment verifies it, saves the result and publishes a PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined event on the broker, which Order receives and acts on.
sonnet.q8: Payment inserts the provider's event id into webhook_inbox, which has a unique constraint; if already present it replies 200 and does nothing. Downstream, every handler checks current status/keys first so repeated events change nothing.
sonnet.q9: The hold is released (stock back on sale). Triggered by Order, on receiving the PaymentDeclined event, making an HTTP release call to Inventory.
sonnet.q10: Inventory checks at claim time whether every line is still free. If so it re-takes the stock and the order is confirmed as normal; otherwise it publishes ClaimFailed and the order is cancelled and fully refunded.
sonnet.q11: The refund row becomes REFUND_FAILED with attempt count and next retry time; a timer retries every minute until it succeeds, ops are alerted after N attempts (N not decided), and it is never deleted or given up on. It is tracked in Payment's refunds table.
sonnet.q12: The Cart service empties the cart, in reaction to the OrderConfirmed event published by Order (emptying is safe to repeat).
